Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
FORCEPS, PUNCH, CERVICAL BIOPSY 



( Reaffirmed 1997) 



1. Scope — Dimensional and other requirements for cervical punch biopsy forceps used In 
obstetrics. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1. 

2.1 A deviation of ± 2*5 percent shall be allowed on all dimensions. 

3. Material — Stainless steel conforming to Designation 40Crl3 for the cutting jaws and 20Cr13 or. 
30Cr13 for the rest, of IS : 6603-1972 ' Specification for stainless steel bars and flats '. 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The forceps shall be free from scale, burrs, pits, tool marks and other surface defects. 

4.2 All edges shall be smoothly rounded off except the cutting edge. 

4.3 The jaws shall open and close fully and freely without any stiffness. 

4.4 Forceps shall be polished bright and passivated. 

5. Heat Treatment 

5.1 The forceps shall be hardened and tempered to give a hardness of 400 to 460 HV, The cutting 
jaws shall have a hardness of 540 to 600 HV, 

6. Tests 

6-1 Performance — The forceps punch shall be made to punch a card-board sheet 1/2 mm thick. 
The forceps shall do this easily and cleanly. This shall be repeated 10 times. During or on 
completion of the test, the cutting edges of the forceps shall show no sign of damage. 

6.2 Flexibility Test — The flexibility shall be tested in the following manner. 

6.2.1 The jaws shall be made to bite a piece of firm rubber about 1*5 mm thick and the finger 
loops closed as fully as possible. On release, the forceps shall not show any sign of damage or the 
upper jaw shall not become loose at its hinge. 

6-2.2 A force of moderate degree by the fingers shall be applied to the shank attempting to bend 
the shank on the width. This shall be repeated at several points along the shank. The test shall 
then be repeated in a plane at right ahglf s to the first. On completion of the test, the shank shall 
not have acquired permanent set. '^V 

6.3 Corrosion Resistance — The instrument shall safisf^the boiling and autoclaving test as in 
15:7531-1975 'Method of boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of stainless steel 
surgical instruments'. 

6.4 Subject to agreement between the purchaser and th" supplier the instrument may be put to the 
following test: 

Copper Sulphate Test — Scrub the sample with soap and warm water, rinse in hot water and 
then dip in 95 percent ethyl alcohol. Dry the sample. Immerse in copper sulphate solution at 
room temperature for 6 min and wash off with fresh water or wet cotton wool. Composition of 
the solution shall be as follows: 

Copper sulphate ( CUSO4.5H2O ) 4-0 g 

Sulphuric acid ( HgSO/i) (sp gr 1-84) lO'O g 

Distilled water [ see IS :^ 1070-1960 Specification for 
water, distilled quality ( revised) ] 90*0 mi 

No red stains or spots on the sample shall be allowed but dulling of the polished surface may 
be permitted.

7. Marking — Mark with the following: 

a) Manufacturer's name, initial^ or recognized trade-mark; and 

b) The words * stainless steel *., 

7.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

E. Packing — The forceps shall be wrapped in moisture-proof paper or packed in polyethylene bag. 
Each forceps shall then be packed in cartons. The packing may also be done as agreed to between 
the purchaser and the supplier.
